goal: Meet S2 of docs/specs/drive-always-lanes.spec.md: for a single-task Lane the runtime itself spawns one non-interactive Executor (claude --print or pi --print) chosen by Lane Preferences, waits for it inside the Host tool call, re-attaches across wait windows, can stop it, and records a generation-bound exit observation taken only from its own child-process exit event (Spec D3, D4, D8, settlement enumeration).

acceptance.assertion: For a single-task Lane the runtime spawns exactly one Executor process with the Lane as cwd and the Executor Host's drive entry for task_id as its only prompt: claude-code as claude --print with --plugin-dir of the loaded plugin directory and, when resolved, --model and --effort; pi as pi --print with, when resolved, --model and --thinking. Host, model and effort resolve per field from the literal request, the selected user Lane profile, project lanes defaults, then the Parent's own Host; a model or effort from a layer other than its executor_host's is dropped and reported not_applied (BR-REQ-6). HERDR_ENV=1 does not change the spawn and no Herdr tab is created (BR-DEC-4). Refusals that spawn nothing: lanes.valid false, and an Executor binary that is not on PATH (lane_executor_unavailable, with no substitute Host, detached job or in-process subagent). Seam: tests/lane-supervisor.test.ts with fake claude and pi executables that record their argv and cwd, plus the adapter tests on both Hosts.

The single-task call blocks until the spawned generation exits or a per-Host wait window elapses. On exit it records {repository, lane path, generation, pid, exit code or signal} from the runtime's own child exit event and then reads the Lane Kernel projection; exit code 0 with a Lane record that is not done is not settlement, and a non-zero exit with a done record still settles. On window elapse it returns lane_supervision.state running for the same generation, and the next call re-attaches without a second spawn, so a Lane never has two live generations. After the Host process lost its handle (a fresh adapter instance with a recorded live generation) the call returns lane_executor_unobservable, records the exit as unknown and spawns nothing while that pid is alive. A generation that ends without Kernel progress is relaunched once as generation N+1; a second end without progress parks needs_human with lane_executor_no_progress. Each Host's window is a named constant that a test pins below that Host's tool-call limit, verified during implementation (Spec D4). Live, exited and unknown processes are tested for both the claude-code and pi providers. Seam: tests/lane-supervisor.test.ts with real child processes from fake executables.

A single-task call with stop: true terminates the current generation with SIGTERM and, after a bounded grace period, SIGKILL, and records stopped_by_parent; cancelling the waiting call through its AbortSignal does the same and records interrupted. Neither observation, nor a timeout, counts as a normal exit, and a stop with no live generation changes nothing and reports so. Batch (Initiative) supervision and its handoffs are unchanged. Seam: tests/lane-supervisor.test.ts and the adapter tests on both Hosts.
